stem.en: Kabir says: "A family with four daughters is more likely to have a son next, to even it out." What does the square say?

text.en: Each fertilisation is a fresh toss. The father's sperm carries X or Y half the time regardless of past children. The fifth child is a boy with the same one-in-two chance as the first.

feedback.en: Chromosomes have no memory of earlier children. The square is the same every time.
Four daughters in a row happens one family in sixteen by chance alone, no tendency needed.
The mother gives X every time. Only the sperm varies.

explanation.en: Independent tosses. Past outcomes do not change the next square. A run of one sex is ordinary chance.
